display.purpose: The heading panel only: "Tasks" alone before there are tasks (3rem / 3.75rem from sm), then "Tasks" over the urgency line at equal size (1.5rem on phones / 2.25rem from sm).

stat.purpose: Overview counts; they count up on show and change. 1.5rem on phones, 2.25rem from sm.

headline.purpose: Dialog and page titles; all h1–h3 use Gabarito.

title.purpose: Task titles, clamped to two lines.

field-label.purpose: Form field labels (labelText) and the editor's More details row, 13px medium: between Body and Label.

label.purpose: Chips, badges, metadata, counts, kbd keys and the Trash count. Nothing is set below 12px.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Cards at rest: empty in light, a faint top highlight in dark. Never `none`.

shadows.name: shadow-pop
shadows.purpose: Hovered cards, the focused quick add, toasts.

shadows.name: shadow-modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, over a 50% near-black backdrop with a 6px blur.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--bg)
shadows.purpose: Two-tone focus on every control; visible on any panel colour.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances, reveals and the theme fade.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Exits and small state changes (exits stay at or under 250ms).

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Hover and focus colour/border transitions, the backdrop fade.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Entrances, reveals, the header slide, the theme fade.

motion.name: duration-count
motion.purpose: Number count-ups and the meter fill.

motion.name: duration-float
motion.purpose: One bob of a decorative empty-state icon (motion-safe only).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all durations 0ms; final state at once
motion.purpose: Guaranteed by MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" and a global CSS override.

components.name: Brand Button
components.description: The single most prominent action per screen (New task). Orange panel that lights up mustard on hover.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main action inside dialogs (Save). Burnt orange, darker on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Save</button>

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral filled action in the well-stone tone.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-secondary">Cancel</button>

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Quiet text action that gains a fill on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost">Remind me later</button>

components.name: Danger Solid Button
components.description: The go-ahead inside a destructive confirmation (Delete forever, Replace everything). Solid danger red with white ink, darker on hover; never anywhere else.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-danger-solid">Delete forever</button>

components.name: Field
components.description: Flat filled well; the border and a soft orange glow appear on hover and focus. Placeholders in full Weathered Grey (4.5:1 or better). With an error, a danger border that stays on hover and focus, and the message right under it, read out as an alert.
components.html: Effort should look like 30m, 2h or 1h30m.

components.name: Date Field
components.description: A deadline or reminder date typed day first (DD/MM/YYYY) in a Field well, in tabular figures, with the native picker behind a 32px muted icon button inside the right edge that hovers to the seam colour. Short forms and words ("8/3", "fri 5pm") are written back in full on leaving the field; a 12px muted line under it confirms the reading as it is typed. The time sibling is the same with a clock and HH:MM.
components.html: Due Fri 13/03/2026, 17:30 · In 3 days

components.name: Quick Add Syntax
components.description: The quick-add grammar on demand. A 36px muted circle-help button inside the bar's right edge ("Quick add syntax") opens a 320px Lifted White popover with the pop shadow, 8px under the quick-add panel and lined up with its right edge; Esc or a tap elsewhere closes it. A bold 14px title, then a two-column list: each token as a 12px Well Stone chip, its name in semibold and the other forms it takes in muted text with the tokens in ink, then "The rest of the line is the title." The keyboard shortcuts sheet shows the same list. Rows come from QUICK_ADD_SYNTAX, and a unit test parses every token shown.
components.html:
Quick add syntax

#finance
Tag. Add as many as you like.
@home
Project. One per task.
!high
Priority. Also !low, !med or !urgent.
~30m
Effort. Also ~2h or ~1h30m.
fri 5pm
Deadline. Also tomorrow, in 3 days or 25/12 17:30. Day first.

The rest of the line is the title.

components.name: Details Disclosure
components.description: The task editor's More details row: full width, 44px tall, 13px, a semibold name, then a plain-words summary of what's set behind it (fg/80) or, with nothing set, what's there (muted), and a muted chevron at the right that turns over when open. Hover fills it Well Stone. It starts closed every time the editor opens; its fields stay in the DOM and fade up when it opens, and a Save that finds a problem there opens it.

components.name: Header Navigation
components.description: A sticky bar in the solid canvas colour (no see-through blur): brand mark and wordmark, then a neutral tray of header buttons that light up mustard on hover, then New task. The buttons gain their words as the width allows (Backup and Trash from md, Projects & tags and the bell from lg), Trash's count a corner badge at every width (the worded button keeps 18px on its right to clear it), so the tray never shifts. The theme button is a Menu (System, Light, Dark) showing a sun or moon. Under sm the tray keeps the bell and Trash and gathers the rest into a labelled More menu. Touch screens (hover: none) keep that pattern up to lg, with Trash's word from sm; from lg on touch Theme shows its word, and the shortcuts button is never offered on touch. In Trash, New task is hidden but keeps its space, so the tray never moves.
components.html: Task Tracker

components.name: Menu
components.description: A header button that opens a popover menu (WAI-ARIA menu pattern): Lifted White with the pop shadow, 224px, 8px under its button and lined up with its right edge. 40px rows with an 18px icon and 14px medium text, mustard on hover. Choices sit under a 12px semibold muted group label with the pick ticked at the end; no rules. Opens on the pick, arrows/Home/End move, Esc returns to the button, Tab closes. The button stays lit while open.
components.html: Theme

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Pill toggle inside the open filter panel: idle in Well Stone, mustard on hover. Pressed takes its own colour and keeps it under the pointer: the status panel, a label tint, or ink for a priority (Urgent rust). Priority pills carry the priority glyph before the word. The status pills are To Do and In Progress only; “Show completed” alone admits done tasks.

components.name: Active Filter Chip
components.description: A pressed filter shown under the collapsed filter row: the same pill and pressed colour, plus an × that removes it. Hover lifts with the pop shadow, not mustard.

Badges and group tabs are Well Stone, pressed pills ink; Urgent alone is rust.

components.name: Filters Toggle
components.description: The disclosure beside search that holds the filter panel: a 36px well-stone button with a count badge of active filters and a chevron that turns over when open. Inside, the pill groups carry visible names (Priority, Status, Tags) that also label each group; opening it on a short screen scrolls just enough to keep the list's start in view.

components.name: Task Card
components.description: Flat neutral panel; an Urgent task has a 6px rust stripe down its left edge (Low, Medium and High have none; High reads by its glyph and word, so the selection marker is the only ink bar); round complete control (a 44px touch target around the 20px circle), title, then one metadata row in reading order: when (deadline, Repeat), what (priority badge unless Medium: a Well Stone well with the glyph and word, Urgent filled rust; In Progress), labels (@project, tags capped at three with a muted +N chip naming the rest), then muted counts; pops on hover. Overdue is the 2px ring in --alert-outline (the danger colour: #b42318 by day, rose at night) plus the deadline in the same red, with no badge. Selected (J/K or Tab) lifts with the pop shadow and shows a 4px ink marker in the gutter 7px left of the card, never a ring; the title button's own focus ring steps aside while its card is selected. Below sm, tags are a dot and name with no tint or ring and the counts are hidden; grouped by priority, no priority badge. An overdue card also has a small muted Move button at its top right (in place of the hover chevron) opening a menu: Tomorrow, Next week (time of day kept), Pick a date… (the editor at its deadline); T moves the selected task to tomorrow; an ink toast says where it went, with Undo.

Tasks

components.name: Overview Stat Tile
components.description: Colour tile that is also a filter (aria-pressed toggle): label, icon and a big tabular Gabarito count; Completed adds a meter. components.name: Discard Bar
components.description: The task editor’s sticky footer when a close would lose unsaved changes: a Noon Mustard bar with the question, a quiet Discard, a quiet Save on a 10% ink tint so it never reads as Discard (saves and closes, as the footer's would) and the inverted Keep editing, which takes focus. Esc on it means Keep editing.
components.html: Discard your changes?

components.name: Confirm Dialog
components.description: Every “are you sure?” in the app, in place of the browser’s confirm box. A small Lifted White alertdialog: a Headline question, a body with the counts involved (two states compared in a Well Stone list), then Cancel and a go-ahead named for the action. Destructive ones use the solid danger button and focus Cancel first; Esc cancels. Restore's adds a danger warning line (with an icon) when the file has fewer tasks, and a secondary Download current data button that works without closing the question. A file with no tasks gets its own question (“This backup has no tasks”), and undoing a restore after changes asks first (“Undo the restore?”).

Replace everything with this backup?

Your current data will be lost. Download a backup first if you might need it.

components.name: Backup Status
components.description: The state of the data in Backup & restore: a Well Stone list with Last backup (DD/MM/YYYY, 24-hour, or Never) and Storage (Protected, Not protected or Not reported, with a muted line saying what that means). While storage isn't protected, an underlined Burnt Orange Text button asks the browser for it; once granted, focus moves to the answer.

components.name: Toast
components.description: An ink-panel notice (the text colour on the canvas colour, so near-black in light and off-white in dark) that slides in from the screen edge with the pop shadow. A 14px medium message with pretty wrapping (task titles shortened to 60 characters so the words around them always show), an optional regular detail line (“Next due tomorrow 07:00”), an Undo in the ink panel inverted (so the screen keeps one brand-orange button) and a quiet Dismiss. It closes after 6 seconds, waiting while the pointer is over it, focus is inside it or a dialog is open over it; a failure toast (role=alert) stays until dismissed, as does a sticky one whose action lasts the session (Undo restore after Backup & restore closes). Status toasts are read out through an always-present live region. Completion toasts share one slot; Z runs the newest Undo.
components.html:
Done: Morning run

Next due tomorrow 07:00

components.name: Square Checkbox
components.description: The square sibling of the round task checkbox, for everything that isn’t completing a task (Show completed, checklist items): 16px, 4px corners, a 1.5px Weathered Grey border that meets 3:1, the same soft sage hover halo, sage fill and ink tick (sage means done). Round always means “complete this task”.
components.html: <label class="ds-boxcheck-row"><input type="checkbox" class="ds-boxcheck" checked> Show completed (2)</label>

components.name: Label Row
components.description: One project or tag in Projects & tags: a round 28px colour swatch (the label’s dot made big, with a faint inner ring) that opens a popover radio group of the seven calm label colours (each 30° of hue clear of danger, brand, mustard, violet and done; arrows pick, Enter/Space/click pick and close, Esc cancels, leaving focus closes; the pick has a dark check and an inner ring), its name in a field well with its muted sigil (@ or #) right against it, so it reads as editable (saves on blur or Enter), the number of tasks it’s on (also the field’s description), and Delete.
components.html: 4 tasks

narrative.overview:
The app is a warm, physical surface where one person lays out their work. The canvas is a sun-warmed off-white by day and near-black by night. On it sit flat, saturated colour panels, like tiles set out on a bench, each one a tool or a reading ready to pick up. The signature is the heading panel: a big orange slab with "Tasks" set heavy in Gabarito and a black sun that rises into its corner on load. Once there are tasks, the slab speaks for urgency: a second display line under "Tasks" says what needs attention ("2 overdue"). Everything else stays quieter than that one moment.

The panels carry meaning, not decoration. Colour says how urgent something is (maroon overdue, mustard due today, violet open, sage done), so the bench reads at a glance before any text does. Separation comes from colour and the gutters between tiles, never from hairline borders or heavy drop shadows. Density is standard rather than compact: a phone-sized glance and a desk-sized planning session should both feel unhurried.

Controls are **calm and confident**. They stay flat and quiet at rest and answer clearly on hover and focus: a mustard light-up, a soft lift, a strong two-tone focus ring. Motion is expressive (panels rise in, the completion burst, count-ups), but always on top of a guaranteed reduced-motion state where everything appears finished at once. Sill's photography, handwriting font, illustrated scenes and pinned horizontal scroll are deliberately not part of this world.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, saturated panels on a warm canvas; colour and gutters separate, borders and shadows don't
One soft-square radius (16px) across every panel, so the whole app can be dialled squarer in one place
Heavy Gabarito display for headings and big numbers; Inter for everything you read
Colour is semantic: every meaningful hue comes from the panel palette, each with its paired ink
The same panel palette in light and dark; only the canvas and text invert
Expressive motion with a hard reduced-motion guarantee

rules.name: The Panel Means Something Rule
rules.body: Anything that carries meaning by colour (status, counts, notices) uses a panel with its paired ink. Never a raw hue, never a Tailwind palette colour.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Colour means time and state: maroon overdue, mustard due soon, violet open, sage done. Each of those hues has that one job (mustard's hover light aside), so a colour never needs a legend. Priority isn't a colour: it's the signal-bars glyph and its word, and only Urgent keeps a hue (rust). Notices with no state to show (toasts, the backup reminder) are ink or neutral, not a borrowed panel.

rules.name: The Readable Label Rule
rules.body: User-picked project and tag colours appear only as a dot, a 16% tint and an inset ring. Text on them stays in the body colour, because a user's light hue as text drops to 2:1.

rules.name: The Paired Ink Rule
rules.body: Every panel/ink pair meets 4.5:1. When a source swatch failed, the ink or the swatch was moved, never the standard. New pairs prove themselves in `e2e/contrast.spec.ts` before they ship.

rules.name: The Heavy Headline Rule
rules.body: Gabarito is for headings, the wordmark and big numbers only, and always at bold or extra-bold. Anything you read in sentences is Inter.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes in place (stats, percentages, counts in tabs and badges) uses tabular figures so it doesn't jitter.

rules.name: The Urgency-First Rule
rules.body: The first screen answers "what needs me now?" before anything else. At 1024×768 and up, the first task card is on the first screen even with the backup reminder showing; on a 390×844 phone it is on the first screen once the reminder is dismissed. `e2e/layout.spec.ts` guards both. Controls that refine the list stay collapsed by default so they never push it down.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow just for existing. If a shadow appears, something was hovered, focused or opened.

rules.name: The Empty Shadow Rule
rules.body: A "no shadow" token is `0 0 #0000`, never `none`. Tailwind merges shadows and rings into one list, and `none` would void the overdue ring and the picked tile's outline.

rules.name: The One Form Rule
rules.body: On a card, each mark takes its own shape: an edge stripe for Urgent, a ring for overdue, a gutter marker for selection. Never reuse one form for two meanings.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Panels never invent their own radius. They use `rounded-panel`, and the inner steps above are the only other corners in the system.

dos: **Do** take every colour, radius, shadow and duration from `src/index.css`, `src/ui.ts` and `presets.ts`.
**Do** carry meaning with a `panel.*` colour and its paired ink, and prove new pairs at 4.5:1 in both themes.
**Do** keep panels flat and separated by 12px gutters; reserve shadows for hover, focus and open dialogs.
**Do** use `rounded-panel` (16px) on every panel, and the inner steps (12 / 8 / 6 / 4px) only inside them.
**Do** show selection with an outline ring, not colour alone, and keep the two-tone focus ring visible on every control.
**Do** keep exactly one brand-orange button per screen.
**Do** light up coloured controls Noon Mustard on hover (`hoverHighlight`).
**Do** animate movement with `transform` and `opacity` only, and guarantee a final-state render under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use hairline borders or heavy drop shadows as separators.
**Don't** use raw hues for meaning, or a user-picked colour as text.
**Don't** use ad-hoc durations, easings, colours or radii outside the tokens and presets.
**Don't** use `transition-all`, or animate `width`, `height`, `top` or `left`; scale a bar instead.
**Don't** use GSAP, ScrollTrigger, Lenis or any scroll hijacking.
**Don't** load fonts or libraries from a CDN at runtime; the app must look the same offline.
**Don't** remove the focus outline (`outline: none`) or show selection by colour alone.
**Don't** bring in Sill's photography, handwriting font, illustrated hero scenes or pinned horizontal scroll.
**Don't** set body text, labels or long strings in Gabarito.
